map_lists:
- Indent lines with a single tab character per indenting level.
- Use Unix-style newlines (single LF character).
- Ensure all files end with a newline.
- Encode all text files with UTF-8 without a Byte Order Mark.
- Avoid adding trailing whitespace.
- Do not use parentheses with keywords where they are not necessary.
- Place braces on the same line as the start of the function, conditional, or loop.
- Place else/elseif on the same line as the previous closing brace.
- Indent multi-line statements by one extra level for the second and subsequent lines.
- Avoid vertical alignment.
- Use spaces rather than tabs for mid-line vertical alignment when needed.
- Break lines between 80 and 100 columns.
- Place the operator separating two lines consistently at the end or start of the line.
- Put the method operator at the beginning of the next line.
- Do not write control structure blocks as a single line.
- Never build URLs manually with string concatenation.
- Use appropriate API methods (e.g., Linker, Title, mw.util.getUrl) to construct URLs.
- Name server-side code files in UpperCamelCase.
- Name files after the most important class they contain.
- Treat acronyms and abbreviations as single words in CamelCase (e.g., HtmlId).
- Name access point files (e.g., index.php) in lowercase.
- Name maintenance scripts in lowerCamelCase.
- Name files intended for site administrators (e.g., readmes) in UPPERCASE.
- Never include spaces in file names or directories.
- Never use non-ASCII characters in file names.
- Use hyphens instead of underscores for lowercase titles.
- Place JavaScript, CSS, and media files in a directory named after the module bundle.
- Name JavaScript files that define classes to match the class name exactly.
- Register extension module bundles with names like ext.myExtension.
- Include a license header at the top of every source file.
- Refer to licenses by their full name or acronym as per SPDX standard.
- Avoid dynamically constructing identifiers such as interface message keys, CSS class names, or file names.
- Write out identifiers and select between them using conditionals or switches.
- Leave a comment with possible values if concatenating identifiers with variables is necessary.
- Document all significant changes in the RELEASE-NOTES-N.NN file.
- Include Phabricator task IDs at the start of release note entries if applicable.
- Add new release note entries in chronological order at the end of the section.
- Use hyphens instead of CamelCase or snake_case for new system message keys.
- Do not hardcode colons in system messages used as labels.
- Use message keys as whole strings in code rather than building them on the fly.
- Use American English spelling for messages, comments, and documentation.
- Add punctuation to non-title error messages.
- Prefer improving core components over duplicating code in extensions.
- Refactor code as changes are made.
- Use separate commits for large refactoring efforts.
- Use reserved data attributes (data-ooui, data-parsoid, data-mw) to distinguish trusted HTML sources.

- Reference code entities exactly as they appear in the code.
- Use quotes around code entity names that start with a lowercase letter.
- Use sentence case for all headings and page titles.
- Write the first line of a method doc-block in the imperative mood to describe what the method does in one sentence.
- Separate additional text in a method doc-block from the first line with an empty line.
- Start parameter descriptions with a capital letter.
- Omit "a" or "the" at the beginning of parameter descriptions.
- Include a period at the end of a parameter description only if it contains multiple sentences.

- Indent with tabs, not spaces.
- Limit lines to 120 characters.
- Put spaces on either side of binary operators.
- Put spaces next to parentheses on the inside, except where the parentheses are empty.
- Do not put a space following a function name.
- Put a space after the : in the function return type hint, but not before.
- Put spaces in brackets when declaring an array, except where the array is empty.
- Follow control structures (if, while, for, foreach, switch, catch) with a space.
- Do not use a space within or after the cast operator when type casting.
- Put one space between the # or // character and the comment in comments.
- Use if blocks instead of multi-line ternary operators.
- Place the question mark and colon at the beginning of the second and third lines in multi-line ternary expressions.
- Prefer single quotes for string literals where equivalent to double quotes.
- Avoid passing huge numbers of parameters to functions or constructors.
- Avoid using boolean parameters in functions.
- Do not repurpose variables over the course of a function.
- Avoid modifying parameters passed to a function unless passed by reference.
- Do not use assignment as an expression.
- Use string literals instead of constants for enum-like sets.
- Use lowercase for true, false, and null.
- Use elseif instead of else if.
- Avoid alternative syntax for control structures; use braces instead.
- Prefer arrow functions for single-line anonymous functions.
- Use native type declarations and return type declarations when applicable.
- Use PHP 7.1 syntax for nullable parameters.
- Do not add PHPDoc comments that only repeat native types.
- Treat acronyms and abbreviations as single words in CamelCase naming.
- Prefix top-level functions with wf.
- Prefix global extension functions with ef.
- Use verb phrases for function names.
- Mark functions exposed for testing as @internal.
- Prefix global variables with $wg.
- Place global declarations at the beginning of a function.
- Name Database objects for writing $dbw.
- Name Database objects for non-concurrency-sensitive reading $dbr.
- Avoid using $ws, $wc, $wp, and $m prefixes in new code.
- Use empty() only to suppress errors; otherwise use boolean conversion.
- Do not use isset() to test for null; use === null instead.
- Do not use ! or empty to test if a string or array is empty; use === '' or === [] instead.
- Use array_merge() instead of array plus to renumber keys.
- Set error_reporting() to -1.
- Omit trailing ?> tags in pure PHP files.
- Do not use the goto syntax.
- Do not pass by reference when traversing an array with foreach unless necessary.
- Do not use static variables within non-static methods.
- Prefer triple-equals (===) over double-equals (==) for comparisons.
- Use == to check equality of scalars that are supposed to be numeric.
- Provide the third parameter to in_array.
- Do not use Yoda conditionals.
- Represent potentially large integers as strings in JSON.
- Do not use PHP's built-in serialize() and unserialize() for data stored outside the current process.
- Use JSON-based serialization instead of PHP serialization.
- Do not add type declarations for big legacy classes (Title, Article, WikiPage, User, MediaWiki, OutputPage, WebRequest, EditPage).
- Omit explicit type declarations for DOM classes or use Wikimedia\Parsoid\DOM\Document aliases.
- Include Doxygen-style comments for new classes, methods, and member variables.
- Document parameters and return values for all new methods.
- Begin Doxygen comments with /**.
- Use @ rather than \ as the escape character for Doxygen tags.
- Provide a @since VERSION tag for every public interface added or changed.
- Use FIXME for bad or broken code, TODO for needed improvements, and HACK for suboptimal solutions.
- Include a license header at the top of every source file.
- Use Doxygen tags in the specified order.
- Mark code as private unless there is a reason to make it more visible.
- Do not access PHP superglobals directly; use $request->get*() methods.
- Do not access $_SERVER directly; use $request->getIP() for IP addresses.
- Use static::func() for calling overridable static methods from inside a class.
- Use self::func() for calling static methods that may not be overridden.
- Use parent::func() for calling a parent method from an override.
- Do not write out the class name like ClassName::func() for static method calls.
- Use :: for

- Use ESLint with the eslint-config-wikimedia preset for code quality and style enforcement.
- Configure ESLint with "root": true in .eslintrc.json to prevent unintended configuration inheritance.
- Use tabs for indentation.
- Do not use trailing whitespace.
- Use blank lines to separate logically related blocks of code.
- Use one space on both sides of binary and assignment operators.
- Separate keywords followed by a left parenthesis with one space.
- Do not place a space between a function name and its left parenthesis.
- Use one space inside parentheses for if statements, function calls, and argument lists.
- Do not use operators (delete, void, typeof, new, return) as if they are functions.
- Wrap lines at no more than 80–100 characters.
- Indent statement continuations one extra level.
- Place function calls and objects on a single line or split them with one segment per line.
- Align closing parentheses with their opening counterparts.
- Wrap individual JavaScript files in an immediately-invoked function expression (IIFE) if not using package files.
- Declare variables before use.
- Place each assignment on its own line.
- Declare functions before use.
- Place function declarations after variable declarations and before main statements in the function body.
- Place comments on their own line above the code they describe.
- Separate comment syntax from text with a single space.
- Start comment text with a capital letter.
- End valid sentence comments with a full stop.
- Use line comments (//) within functions and code blocks.
- Use block comments (/* */) only for documentation blocks.
- Use sentence case for text in free-form documentation blocks.
- Indent continued sentences in annotations with one additional space.
- Use @classdesc to document ES5 classes and @description for their constructors.
- Use separate comments to document ES6 classes and their constructors.
- Use JSDoc for building documentation.
- Use strict equality operators (=== and !==) instead of loose equality.
- Do not use Yoda conditionals.
- Use typeof val === 'string' for string type checks.
- Use typeof val === 'number' for number type checks.
- Use typeof val === 'boolean' for boolean type checks.
- Use typeof val === 'function' for function type checks.
- Use val === Object( val ) for object type checks.
- Use jQuery.isPlainObject( val ) for plain object type checks.
- Use Array.isArray( val ) for array type checks.
- Use obj.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE for HTMLElement type checks.
- Use val === null for null type checks.
- Use val === undefined for undefined type checks.
- Use single quotes for string literals.
- Use the slice() method to extract parts of strings.
- Avoid using substr() or substring() methods.
- Access browser globals (document, navigator, URL, fetch) directly rather than as properties of window.
- Access window properties (location, history, name) as properties of window, not as bare globals.
- Avoid creating new global variables.
- Avoid modifying globals not owned by your code.
- Do not extend built-in globals like String or Object with utility methods.
- Use module.exports or the mw hierarchy to publicly expose functionality.
- Access MediaWiki configuration variables via mw.config.
- Do not modify built-in prototypes such as Object.prototype.
- Name variables using CamelCase starting with a lowercase letter.
- Name constant variables using all caps with underscores for separation.
- Name functions using CamelCase starting with a lowercase letter.
- Name class constructors using CamelCase starting with an uppercase letter.
- Start method names with a verb.
- Treat acronyms in names as normal words, uppercasing only the first letter as needed.
- Prefix variables holding jQuery objects with a dollar sign.
- Publish standalone npm projects under the @wikimedia namespace where appropriate.
- Use the simple <tag> syntax in the jQuery constructor to create plain elements.
- Avoid using for-in loops to iterate over arrays.
- Access localStorage and sessionStorage keys via mw.storage or mw.storage.session.
- Start storage keys with mw and use camel case or hyphens.
- Do not use underscores in storage keys.
- Store values in storage as strings.
- Use "1" or "0" for boolean state in storage.
- Store numbers as-is and cast with Number on retrieval.
- Use comma-separated or pipe-separated strings for lists of software-defined values in storage.
- Use JSON for lists of user-generated or complex values in storage.
- Avoid using user-generated input as part of a storage key name.
- Avoid creating a large number of storage keys; use a single key with LRU strategy if necessary.

- Use the defineComponent() function from Vue for component definitions.
- Write new code using Vue 3 and ES6.
- Use Vue's single-file components format (.vue) wherever possible.
- Follow the Vue community's style guide, specifically all "Priority A: Essential" recommendations.
- Order single-file component sections as <template>, <script>, and <style>.
- List each component file individually under the packageFiles property in extension.json.
- Include the vue module as a dependency in the module definition.
- Do not use self-closing component tags; always include a closing tag.
- Use kebab-case for component tags.
- Use directive short-hands (:foo, @click) instead of full syntax (v-bind:, v-on:).
- Break multiple element attributes onto separate lines.
- Keep template expressions simple; define complex logic as computed properties or methods.
- Internationalize message strings in templates.
- Use v-html sparingly and only after auditing for XSS vulnerabilities.
- Use v-i18n-html instead of v-html for parsed i18n messages where possible.
- Add an eslint-disable-next-line comment if v-html usage is verified as safe.
- Use CommonJS module format with module.exports and require() for components delivered via ResourceLoader.
- Order component options as: name, components, mixins, props, emits, setup, data, computed properties, methods, watchers, lifecycle hooks, and render functions.
- Avoid render functions; prefer HTML-style templates.
- Define prop defaults and validation where necessary.
- Default boolean props to false.
- Avoid implicit parent-child communication and mutation of received props.
- Prefer the "props down / events up" approach for component communication.
- Nest styles under a single selector if using LESS.
- Use conditional CSS classes for dynamic styles.
- Use object syntax for computed properties bound to class attributes.
- Follow CSS class naming patterns for Vue transition names, including extension-specific prefixes.

- Indent lines with 4 spaces.
- End files with a newline.
- Keep lines under 80 characters long.
- Organize imports in alphabetical order.
- Separate standard library, third party, and local library imports with empty lines.
- Include docstrings for all but the simplest functions.
- Append an underscore to variable names that conflict with builtins.

- Adopt the role/profile pattern for organizing new code into modules, profiles, and roles.
- Ensure any node declaration includes only one role invoked with the role function.
- Prevent classes, defines, or resources in modules from using classes from other modules.
- Avoid using defines from other modules within a module wherever possible.
- Prohibit explicit or implicit hiera calls within modules.
- Set profile class parameters only via explicit lookup calls, optionally providing a default value.
- Deprecate the use of legacy hiera functions (hiera, hiera_hash, hiera_include).
- Prohibit hiera calls outside of profile class parameters.
- Instantiate classes explicitly in profiles rather than using the include class method, except for specific global classes.
- List profile preconditions using the require keyword at the start of the class.
- Include profiles in roles only via the include keyword and a system::role definition.
- Prohibit conditionals and hiera calls within roles.
- Discourage inheritance between roles.
- Include the standard profile in all roles.
- Prohibit class parameter autolookup; explicitly declare variables as parameters in profile classes.
- Define hiera calls only in profiles as default values of class parameters.
- Define hiera definitions for parameters in the role hierarchy, reserving the common hierarchy for shared data structures.
- Limit per-host hiera usage to testing tweaks or canary declarations, not for adding or subtracting functionality.
- Name hiera keys to reflect the most specific common shared namespace of the puppet classes looking them up.
- Avoid global variables in hiera; use snake case and no semicolons for global keys.
- Define nodes in site.pp as simple one-liners including the role class.
- Include the base class for every node.
- Use a system::role definition for every deployed service to indicate what the server is running.
- Set read-only file mode (0444 or 0555) for files fully deployed by Puppet using the file type.
- Create a nested class named profile::service::monitoring for each service to set up monitoring configuration.
- Document top-level class definitions with descriptive headers.
- Use four-space soft tabs for indentation.
- Prohibit the use of literal tab characters.
- Prohibit trailing white space.
- Align fat comma arrows (=>) within blocks of attributes.
- Use single quotes for strings unless interpolating variables.
- Enclose variables in braces ({}) when interpolating them in a string.
- Do not quote variables standing by themselves.
- Do not quote booleans.
- Single quote all resource names and their attributes, except for ensure and variables.
- Place the ensure attribute first in resource declarations.
- Put a trailing comma after the final resource parameter.
- Prohibit grouping resources of the same type (compression).
- Keep the resource name and resource type on the same line.
- Prohibit the use of selectors inside resources.
- Include default cases in case statements.
- Place all classes and resource type definitions in separate files in the manifests directory.
- Prohibit nesting classes.
- Prohibit the use of inheritance.
- Favor using the facts hash when referring to facts to distinguish them from global variables.
- Refer to global variables using fully qualified names.
- Do not use dashes in class names; prefer alphabetic names only.
- List required parameters before optional parameters in parameterized class and defined resource type declarations.
- Avoid parameters that do not have a default value.
- Place one include per line.
- Include only one class per include statement.
- Include only the specific class needed, not the entire scope.
- Use Debian packages from the WMF apt repo or official upstream Ubuntu repos for software installation.
- Prohibit the use of source-based packaging systems like pip or gem.
- Use the stdlib function ensure_packages for installing apt packages when possible.

- Name classes and IDs using all lowercase letters separated by dashes.
- Prefix classes and IDs with mw- to avoid conflicts with wikitext parser IDs.
- Place one selector and one property per line.
- Place opening braces for CSS declaration blocks on the same line as the last selector.
- Indent property declarations with a tab.
- Do not place a space before the colon.
- Place one space between the colon and the value.
- Place one space after commas in multi-value properties.
- Place a semi-colon after each declaration, including the last one.
- Unindent closing braces to the left.
- Place annotation comments for CSSJanus and CSSMin on their own line above the CSS declaration.
- Place an empty line between CSS rule sets.
- Use url() syntax without quotes in background-image declarations.
- Use lowercase hex colour values, preferring shorthand notation where possible.
- Use rgba() values when alpha transparency is necessary.
- Use the transparent colour keyword.
- Avoid other colour keyword values, rgb(), hsl(), and hsla() notations.
- Ensure colour contrast ratios meet WCAG 2.0 level AA.
- Place newer CSS vendor prefixes after older versions, with the standardized declaration at the end.
- Use the .client-js or .client-nojs class to conditionally style elements based on JavaScript support.
- Avoid using z-index when possible, relying on natural DOM stacking order instead.
- Avoid using !important unless overriding upstream code that uses !important.
- Increase selector specificity by repeating selectors or adding attribute selectors instead of using !important.
- Indent nested Less blocks with one tab.
- Do not space-align declaration values inside Less mixins.
- Do not place spaces on the outside of parameter lists in Less function invocations, mixin uses, or mixin definitions.
- Do not place quotes around parameter values in Less.
- Separate nested CSS rules from parent declarations in Less with one empty line.
- Place @noflip tags on the immediate line above the declaration in Less.
- Omit the .less file extension in Less import statements.
- Use @import in Less only for loading mixins and variables, not for bundling conceptually related stylesheets.
- Name Less mixins using hyphen-case.
- Prefix Less mixin names with mixin-.
- Use semi-colons to separate arguments in Less mixin calls if the arguments contain commas.
- Include a .stylelintrc.json file in the root directory of the repository.
- Do not override the stylelint-config-wikimedia preset configuration except for selector-class-pattern.
- Enforce Stylelint passing by including it in the npm test script.

- Use Maven as the build tool.
- Inherit from the JVM Parent POM.
- Target Java 8 or Java 11.
- Use Caffeine instead of Guava for caching.
- Use Lombok for generating getters, setters, equals, and hashCode methods.
- Use @SneakyThrows to handle checked exceptions.
- Use JSR 305 annotations (@Nonnull, @Nullable, @ParametersAreNonnullByDefault, @Immutable, @ThreadSafe, @NotThreadSafe) to document expected behavior.
- Use Jackson for JSON and XML parsing and serialization.
- Use Apache HttpComponents as the HTTP client.
- Share a single instance of HttpClient within an application.
- Configure a custom User-Agent string for HTTP clients.
- Use JUnit 5 as the unit testing framework where possible.
- Use Mockito for mocking.
- Use WireMock for HTTP mocking.
- Use AssertJ for assertions.
- Avoid null values and prefer Null Objects.
- Expect parameters to be non-null without explicit checks unless they come from an untrusted caller.
- Mark parameters with @Nonnull or @Nullable.
- Use Optionals sparingly.
- Manually define serialVersionUID only when classes are expected to be deserialized and the class or JVM version might change between serialization and deserialization.
- Start manually defined serialVersionUID at 0 and increment it on each change to the class structure.
- Declare constants as public static final with names in capital letters.
- Define dependency versions in the main pom's <dependencyManagement/> section in multi-module projects.
- Specify shared dependency versions as properties.

- Use tabs for indentation.
- Limit the length of a single line.
- Avoid extraneous whitespace when calling a function or subscripting an array or dictionary.
- Do not use spaces immediately before or inside bracketing characters ([, (, { and their matches).
- Avoid putting multiple statements on one line unless the expression is very short.
- Avoid putting multiple statements on one line for multi-clause statements.
- Split large statements over multiple lines with a hanging indent that aligns with the opening delimiter if a single line is too long.
- Place if statement conditions on the next line.
- Define the entry method as unpacking parameters from the frame and passing them to a function with the same name prefixed with a single underscore.
- Use camelCase for function names.

- Use abstract schema for new tables or schema changes.
- Name tables using singular nouns.
- Prefix column names with the table name or an abbreviation of the table name.

- Use minimal code with readability in mind.
- Set SVGO transformPrecision to at least 7.
- Verify visual quality by diffing files before and after using unsafe SVGO plugins.
- Enable the sortAttrs plugin in SVGO.
- Enable the cleanupEnableBackground plugin in SVGO.
- Use pretty output for human-readable code.
- Indent code by tabs.
- Retain xml:space="preserve" attributes.
- Retain XML comments.
- Retain <title> elements.
- Retain newline, carriage return, and tab characters.
- Retain <g> elements.
- Retain visibility="hidden", opacity="0", and display="none" attributes.
- Retain requiredFeatures attributes.
- Retain <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> declarations.
- Retain <defs> elements.
- Retain <rect> elements.
- Retain <style type="text/css"> elements.
- Retain class attributes.
- Retain data-name attributes.
- Retain inkscape:label attributes.
- Retain <rdf:RDF> elements.
- Retain aria-label attributes.
- Retain <inkscape:grid> elements.
- Retain <sodipodi:guide> elements.
- Retain sodipodi:cx, sodipodi:cy, sodipodi:rx, sodipodi:ry, and sodipodi:type="arc" attributes.
- Retain vector-effect attributes.
- Retain inkscape:groupmode="layer" attributes.
- Retain sodipodi:role="line" attributes.
- Remove standalone="no" from XML processing instructions.
- Lowercase hex color values.
- Shorten hex color values where possible (e.g., #fff instead of #FFFFFF).
- Apply common attributes to a parent <g> element or <svg> statement instead of individual elements.
- Rely on default values for fill and stroke-width.
- Prefer specific shape elements like <circle>, <ellipse>, and <rect> over <path> for readability and editability.
- Merge <path> elements where applicable, unless separate editing is required.
- Do not remove redundant ry attributes when identical to rx.
- Remove unnecessary fill-rule and clip-rule attributes.
- Remove IEEE rounding errors from numeric values.
- Align points to a non-fractional pixel grid.
- Use relative commands instead of absolute commands in paths.
- Use scour with --disable-simplify-colors, --disable-style-to-xml, --disable-group-collapsing, --keep-editor-data, --keep-unreferenced-defs, --protect-ids-noninkscape, --disable-embed-rasters, --set-precision=8, and --set-c-precision=8.
- Use svgcleaner with --allow-bigger-file, --indent yes, --resolve-use no, --apply-transform-to-gradients yes, --apply-transform-to-shapes yes, --convert-shapes no, --group-by-style no, --join-arcto-flags no, --join-style-attributes no, --merge-gradients yes, --regroup-gradient-stops yes, --remove-comments no, --remove-declarations no, --remove-default-attributes yes, --remove-desc no, --remove-dupl-cmd-in-paths yes, --remove-dupl-fegaussianblur yes, --remove-dupl-lineargradient yes, --remove-dupl-radialgradient yes, --remove-gradient-attributes yes, --remove-invalid-stops yes, --remove-invisible-elements no, --remove-metadata no, --remove-needless-attributes yes, --remove-nonsvg-attributes no, --remove-nonsvg-elements no, --remove-text-attributes no, --remove-title no, --remove-unreferenced-ids no, --remove-unresolved-classes yes, --remove-unused-coordinates yes, --remove-unused-defs yes, --remove-version yes, --remove-xmlns-xlink-attribute yes, --simplify-transforms yes, --trim-colors yes, --trim-ids no, --trim-paths yes, --ungroup-defs yes, --ungroup-groups no, --use-implicit-cmds yes, --list-separator comma, --paths-to-relative yes, --remove-unused-segments yes, --convert-segments yes, --apply-transform-to-paths yes, --coordinates-precision 2, --paths-coordinates-precision 5, --properties-precision 3, and --transforms-precision 7.

- Avoid extraneous whitespace when calling a function or subscripting an array or dictionary.
- Do not use spaces immediately before or inside bracketing characters ([, (, { and their matches).
- Use abstract schema for new tables or schema changes.
- Name tables using singular nouns.
- Prefix column names with the table name or an abbreviation of the table name.
- Use minimal code with readability in mind.
- Set SVGO transformPrecision to at least 7.
- Verify visual quality by diffing files before and after using unsafe SVGO plugins.
